To believe; to put credence in.

examples.text: Someone said there were over 100,000 people there, but I can't credit that.

glosses: To add to an account.

examples.text: Credit accounts receivable with the amount of the invoice.

glosses: To acknowledge the contribution of.

examples.text: I credit the town council with restoring the shopping district.

glosses: To bring honour or repute upon; to do credit to; to raise the estimation of.

examples.text: You credit the church as much by your government as you did the school formerly by your wit.

examples.text: When Jonathan and the people heard these words they gave no credit into them, nor received them.

glosses: Recognition, respect and admiration.

examples.text: I give you credit for owning up to your mistake.

glosses: Acknowledgement of a contribution, especially in the performing arts.

examples.text: She received a singing credit in last year's operetta.

glosses: Written titles and other information about the TV program or movie shown at the beginning and/or end of the TV program or movie.

examples.text: They kissed, and then the credits rolled.

examples.text: In view of your payment record, we are happy to extend further credit to you.

glosses: The time given for payment for something sold on trust.

examples.text: a long credit or a short credit

glosses: A person's credit rating or creditworthiness, as represented by their history of borrowing and repayment (or non payment).

examples.text: What do you mean my credit is no good?

glosses: An addition to certain accounts; the side of an account on which payments received are entered.

glosses: A source of value, distinction or honour.

examples.text: That engineer is a credit to the team.
